Author: Mysterious Popoto
Name: GPoseStudio
Description: Captures the GPose frame and applies GPoseStudio color/lighting looks. Cosmetic, client-side only. Works alongside Brio/Ktisis.
Changelog:
0.9.13 - A mask's own settings reach the foreground layer. Its field was shared with the whole image rather than copied into the mask, so changing the fog inside one mask changed it everywhere -- in every other mask and outside them all -- and none of it was recorded as belonging to that mask. The foreground layer can now differ inside a mask like every other setting.
0.9.12 - The Looks tab watches its own folder. A look copied in, written by something else, or edited while the game is up now appears in the list on its own, and the one you have loaded is re-read when its file changes, so none of it needs the plugin reloaded. Anything unsaved on screen is left alone and asked about instead, and a reload is one step back with Undo. The Reload button beside the search box does the same immediately.
0.9.11 - Masks get eight new shapes: polygons, stars, wedges of light, stripes, crosses, the subject's edge (a halo just outside the figure or a rim just inside it), a saturation range and noise patches. Every mask can round its corners, tear its edge, feather inward or outward, be weakened, be kept to the subject or to what is behind it, and be mirrored across the frame; frames can glow and cast a drop shadow. Twenty templates set up panels, light and grading layouts in one click. Element layers can follow a mask, moving, turning and resizing with it. Reset look now clears element layers and captions too, and can be undone. A look saved before these options loads its masks with them at their defaults.
0.9.10 - A mask can have its own settings: the same effects with other values inside it, so one side of the frame can be black and white while the other is warm, or a face a stop brighter than the room. Press Edit inside on a mask and every effect control acts inside it; whatever you leave alone keeps following the whole image. Quick buttons for brighter, darker, black and white, warmer and cooler. Works in the saved image, and travels with the look. Masks combine the way you choose: an effect aimed at several can take both, either, only one, or the first minus the rest; masks with their own settings stack in an order you set, or combine or cancel where they overlap. Background B keeps its own stars, haze, glow and embers. Eight masks, A to H, in a panel that lists only the ones in use, with a section per mask and a list of what each is aimed at. A transparent PNG can keep the inside of chosen masks, backdrop and all, instead of cutting around the character, or have masks removed from it, and that choice is saved with the look. Linked masks are placed together, so a layout of several masks moves, turns and resizes as one. Frames can lie on each other in an order you set, and the characters can be cut at the frames with the outlines still passing behind them.
0.9.9 - Masks get five new shapes: rectangle (a diamond when turned), ring, brightness range, colour range and the subject itself, plus one-click set-ups for a face, a diamond, half the frame, highlights, shadows and skin. Any mask can be a frame: a window onto the picture with its own outline, paper or colour outside, and the subject breaking out over the edge. Two diamond frames sets up the classic two-panel layout in one click.
0.9.8 - Orbs: eight shapes including a bladed aperture from three leaves to twelve, their own colour and a spread across it, and a mode needing neither a highlight nor depth. Particles and orbs are still in progress and are not in this build yet.
0.9.7 - Particles sit in the air rather than on the glass: three layers at different focus, sprites that tumble as they fall, and a Solid mode so ash stops glowing. Bokeh needs a highlight to exist, and has a cat's eye. Freeze stops the clock so a still can be composed.
0.9.6 - Snowfall and Ashfall pulled back so the place you are shooting in still shows through them. A new option clears every setting before a look is applied, for the looks that do not mention everything: a saved part, or a file written before half these settings existed.
0.9.5 - Text captions appear in the exported image. They never did: they were an overlay drawn on the game, and the file comes from the GPU, so a caption showed while you posed and was gone from every picture. One rasteriser now feeds both, so the preview is what gets saved. Multiple lines, any installed font, a real outline, and a size that no longer changes with export scale.
0.9.4 - The built-in set rebuilt: 14 looks designed as a set rather than accumulated one at a time, across Portrait, Cinematic, Backdrop, Weather and Stylised. The 26 earlier looks are kept and installable, and never overwritten. The Looks tab is reorganised around the list rather than around the machinery.
